(1) Ran test/oauth-callback-redirect.test.ts and test/oauth-callback.test.ts myself, unmodified: test/oauth-callback-redirect.test.ts:72 'expected 404 to be less than 400'; test/oauth-callback-redirect.test.ts:87 'expected \'/oauth/callback\' to be \'/settings\'' (Received: '/oauth/callback'); test/oauth-callback.test.ts:164 'expected 404 to be less than 400'. The :87 failure is decisive: location read as '' and new URL('', CALLBACK) trivially resolves back to the original request URL -- exactly what happens when an intermediate 3xx's Location header is consumed by auto-following and the final non-redirect response carries none. (2) Confirmed the mechanism at its source, not by inference: node_modules/@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers/types/cloudflare-test.d.ts documents 'SELF: Fetcher' (service-binding-style fetch) as @deprecated in favour of 'import { exports } from "cloudflare:workers"' + 'exports.default.fetch()' -- i.e. exports.default.fetch() is the typed successor to a Fetcher, and Fetcher/service-binding fetches carry the same default redirect:'follow' semantics as global fetch(). (3) Confirmed src/worker/index.ts has no /settings route and ends in app.notFound() -> 404 JSON, and wrangler.jsonc's assets.run_worker_first is exactly ['/api/*','/oauth/*'] -- /settings is deliberately excluded by design (plan Summary + NOT Building), and vitest.config.ts's miniflare block for the 'worker' project configures no assets binding either. So the 404 is a test-harness artifact, not a production defect: a real browser follows the same 302 in production and lands on the SPA shell via not_found_handling:'single-page-application', a path exports.default.fetch() bypasses entirely by calling the Hono app directly. (4) Considered alternatives before concluding: redirect-following is controlled by the CALLER's fetch options, not by any status or Location value the server chooses, so no genuinely-redirecting implementation of PRD AC-3 / User Flow step 4-5 (PRPs/prds/google-calendar-read.prd.md:140-141, confirmed read directly: 'Google redirects to the callback... He is returned to *Hoje*') and plan AC-A2 can satisfy test/oauth-callback-redirect.test.ts:66-73, :75-89 or test/oauth-callback.test.ts:159-168 as currently invoked. A Worker-side /settings handler would both fall outside the plan's Files to Change (settings is explicitly client-only) and still fail :75-89, since the intermediate redirect's Location is unrecoverable from the final response regardless of what the followed request returns. (5) Confirmed the proposed remedy is achievable, not wishful: redirect is a real, typed RequestInit member in this project's own generated worker-configuration.d.ts:1850, so exports.default.fetch(url, {redirect:'manual'}) is directly usable to observe the raw 3xx and its Location. (6) Confirmed src/worker/routes/oauth-callback.ts's change is exactly c.redirect(destination.toString(), 302) -- correct and spec-compliant, satisfying PRD AC-3 (line 65: 'the code is exchanged... the refresh token is persisted... the nonce is marked consumed') and AC-A2 exactly as intended; git status confirms no test file and no diagnostic residue remain in the working tree. (7) This is a genuine EXISTING-test defect, not new coverage (diff touches zero test files) and not PRD ambiguity (AC-3 and User Flow steps 4-5 are unambiguous) -- it is a test-authoring gap around the harness's redirect-following default that the test file's own pre-implementation docstring and the plan's own pre-implementation Risk table both independently assumed away ('a 302 satisfies... status < 400'), a shared good-faith misunderstanding across the pipeline's planning artifacts, not a self-serving implementer claim. The three cited assertions must be corrected (redirect:'manual' or equivalent) by the test-writer/test-reviewer pair; Task 9's implementation is correct as shipped and must not change.

dispute_evidence.claim: Plan Task 9 requires the OAuth callback's success leg to return a redirect to /settings?google=connected. The implementation does exactly that: c.redirect(destination.toString(), 302). However exports.default.fetch(...) -- the cloudflare:workers entrypoint this suite calls -- FOLLOWS redirects by default, like a real Fetcher. The followed request for /settings has no Worker-side handler (it is intentionally a client-only SPA route -- that is the entire point of this phase), so it lands on app.notFound() (src/worker/index.ts, 404) and the final response carries no Location header. Therefore no implementation of a genuine 3xx redirect can satisfy these assertions as written. The implementer proved this by temporarily registering a /settings handler returning 599 and observing the test see 599 -- the harness had silently re-dispatched the followed request. That probe was reverted and src/worker/index.ts is absent from the attempt diff.
dispute_evidence.proposed_resolution: Amend the assertions to observe the redirect without auto-following it (e.g. construct the request with redirect: "manual"), which is the standard Fetch-API mechanism for inspecting a 3xx response's own status and Location. A test-authoring fix; the Task 9 implementation itself should not change.
